learning_objective: 🎯 Understand how independent India navigated the dangerous Cold War world through Non-Alignment, and managed complex relationships and wars with neighbors like China and Pakistan!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Instead of joining the US (capitalist) or USSR (communist) military blocs during the Cold War, India chose to stay independent, promoting world peace and retaining the freedom to take stands on international issues.
A set of five principles of peaceful coexistence signed between India and China, heavily focused on mutual respect for each other's territorial integrity and non-interference.

Despite the 'Hindi-Chini Bhai-Bhai' slogan, border disputes (Aksai Chin and NEFA/Arunachal) and India granting asylum to the Dalai Lama led to a massive Chinese invasion in 1962, dealing a severe blow to India's confidence.

India fought significant wars with Pakistan in 1965 (over Kashmir) and in 1971. The 1971 war ended with a decisive Indian victory and the liberation of East Pakistan, creating the new nation of Bangladesh.
India conducted its first nuclear test in 1974 (Smiling Buddha) for 'peaceful purposes'. India's policy is based on maintaining a credible minimum deterrence with a strict 'No First Use' commitment.

fun_activity.title: 🕊️ The Peace Treaty Architect
fun_activity.instructions: Imagine you are drafting the 'Panchsheel' (Five Principles). Write down 3 rules you would make two hostile countries agree to so they never fight a war against each other again.

exam_tips: 📌 Differentiate between the causes of the 1962 China war (border dispute, Tibet issue) and the 1971 Pakistan war (East Pakistan refugee crisis).
📌 Know the core philosophy behind NAM: It is not neutrality or isolationism; it is about taking active, independent stands on global issues.
📌 Always mention 'No First Use' (NFU) when explaining India's nuclear doctrine.
quick_recap: ⭐ The Bandung Conference of 1955 laid the foundation for the Non-Aligned Movement (NAM).
⭐ The Tashkent Agreement (1966) ended the 1965 Indo-Pak war, signed by Lal Bahadur Shastri.
⭐ The Shimla Agreement (1972) was signed by Indira Gandhi and Zulfikar Ali Bhutto after the 1971 Bangladesh liberation war.
